graderReportSource: container — the deployment module constructs its own containerGraderReportSource over the daemon Docker driver (createDockerContainerRuntime); the digest-pinned grader image runs the swe-rebench harness (apply patch, run the declared transitions) and leaves grader-output.json on the writable bind-mounted workdir, which the adapter reads

verdict.pass: every declared fail-to-pass transition now passes and no declared pass-to-pass transition broke
verdict.fail: at least one declared transition did not hold
verdict.ungradeable: the grader could not determine the transitions (e.g. pytest missing, container crash) — never a failing verdict, the attempt is retried

scoring.rule: passed = every fail-to-pass node satisfied AND no pass-to-pass node broken

isolation.rationale: the swe-rebench-v2 grade path writes into the image rootfs at grade time — `python3 -m ensurepip --upgrade` and `python3 -m pip install pytest` land in the image's Python site-packages (see operator/src/harnesses/impls/swe-rebench-v2-evaluator/eval-runner.ts PYTEST_INSTALL_GUARD), which lives on the rootfs, not under the writable bind-mounted workdir. A read-only rootfs would fail these installs on any instance whose base image lacks pytest. The container is still resource-capped and confined (--network none, --cap-drop ALL, --no-new-privileges, --pids-limit, --memory, --cpus, noexec/nosuid /tmp) per the driver defaults.

evidence: the adapter attaches the (tail-capped) test log as claim evidence; the deployment's evidenceWriter is a real, durable content-addressed filesystem repository
